query_text: Create a CSS property quick-reference card app for my phone where I can look up any CSS property fast — it shows the property name, what it does, the values it accepts, and a small example, all organized into categories like layout, typography, and colors so I can find things without scrolling forever.

Build a historical figure and contribution card app for my phone that lets me flip through cards one at a time, where each card shows the person's name, their time period, what they're known for, and their key contribution, and I can organize cards by subject like science, art, or politics so I can review them in order.

Create a language verb conjugation flashcard app for my phone that covers all the main tenses — present, past, future — and shows the verb on one side so I can guess the conjugation before tapping to flip it over and check, with a way to mark cards I keep getting wrong so I can focus on those.

A medical terminology spaced repetition deck app for my phone where each card shows a term on the front and the definition, pronunciation, and a short usage example on the back, with cards grouped by body system so I can work through one category at a time and track how many I've mastered in each group.

Create a legal case principle memorization card app for my phone that shows the case name and the legal principle it established on each card, with cards sorted by area of law like contracts, torts, and constitutional law, and a simple way to mark each card as learned or still practicing so I can see my progress by category.

Make a high school physics formula application test app for my phone that covers the main topics like motion, forces, energy, and waves, where each question gives me a real-world scenario and I have to pick the right formula and solve for the answer, with a running score so I can see how many I get right per topic.

Create a university entrance essay planning prompt planner for my phone that walks me through the key steps one at a time — choosing a topic, writing a hook, outlining main points, and drafting a conclusion — and lets me save my notes for each step so I can come back and keep working on it without losing what I wrote.

Build a SAT and ACT full practice simulation app for my phone that lets me pick which test I want to practice and runs through a full timed section with multiple-choice questions, shows me which answers I got wrong at the end, and keeps a record of my scores so I can see if I'm improving over time.

An IELTS and TOEFL writing task drill app for my phone that gives me a practice prompt, lets me type my response in a text box with a timer running, then shows me a sample answer and a checklist of things to look for like thesis clarity, paragraph structure, and vocabulary range so I can compare and learn from it.

Create a medical license USMLE question bank app for my phone that lets me do a practice set of questions by subject — like anatomy, pharmacology, or pathology — with four answer choices each, and after I finish a set it shows me which ones I missed with a short explanation so I know why the right answer is correct.

A recipe skill-unlock tracker app for my phone where I can check off cooking techniques as I learn them — things like knife skills, sautéing, and baking bread — grouped into beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels, and each skill links to the recipe I used to practice it so I have a record of what I've actually made.

Make a dance technique video milestone tracker app for my phone that lets me list the moves and techniques I'm working on, mark each one as in progress or done, and attach a short note about when I hit the milestone, with everything organized by style like hip-hop, contemporary, or ballet so I can track progress in each area separately.

Need a language CEFR level progress tracker app for my phone that shows all six levels from A1 to C2 and lets me check off skills — reading, writing, speaking, listening — as I feel confident in them at each level, with a simple visual showing how far along I am so I can see which areas I've covered and what's still left.

A coding bootcamp daily milestone tracker app for my phone where I can list each day's topic or project, check it off when I finish, and add a short note about what I learned or what tripped me up, with a running count of how many days I've completed so I can see my streak and stay on track with the course schedule.

A reading 52-book annual challenge log app for my phone where I can add each book I finish with the title, author, and the date I completed it, see a running count of how many books I've read out of 52, and browse my list organized by month so I can look back at what I read each month throughout the year.

Build a peer-review assignment submission and rubric app for my phone where students can submit their work and then review a classmate's submission using a clear checklist of criteria with a rating for each item, and once the review is done the original student can see the feedback organized by criteria so everything is in one place and easy to read.

Build a class schedule and module calendar planner for my phone that shows all my classes for the week in a clear day-by-day layout, lets me tap on any class to see the module topic and any notes for that session, and highlights upcoming deadlines so I always know what's coming up this week and next.

Create a mobile app for browsing an online university course catalog where I can filter courses by subject area and level, tap on any course to see the full description, credit hours, and prerequisites, and save the ones I'm interested in to a shortlist so I can compare them later before deciding what to enroll in.

Create a K-12 subject curriculum map app for my phone that lays out all the subjects — math, science, language arts, social studies — by grade level, so I can tap on any grade and subject to see the list of topics covered that year, and check off topics as we go through them to keep track of where we are in the curriculum.

A coding bootcamp module guide app for my phone that lists all the tracks and their modules in order, shows which ones I've completed and which are up next, and lets me tap into any module to see a brief description and the key skills it covers, so I always know exactly where I am in the program and what's coming up.

Need a machine learning model comparison tool for my phone that lists common models like linear regression, decision trees, random forest, and neural networks side by side, showing for each one what type of problem it handles, its main pros and cons, and when to use it, so I can pull it up fast during class or when I'm studying.

Build a road sign quick reference app for my phone that shows every standard road sign with a clear image and a plain-English explanation of what it means, organized by category like warning signs, regulatory signs, and guide signs, so I can look up any sign fast when I'm studying for my driving test.

Create a physics constants and formula quick reference tool for my phone that lists all the key constants like the speed of light and gravitational constant alongside the main formulas grouped by topic — mechanics, electricity, thermodynamics — so I can look up exactly what I need during homework without flipping through my whole textbook.

Build a chemical periodic element reference app for my phone that shows every element with its symbol, atomic number, atomic mass, and the group it belongs to, and lets me tap on any element to see a few quick facts like its common uses and whether it's a metal or nonmetal, so I can look things up fast while studying for chemistry.

A grammar and punctuation rules reference app for my phone that covers the most common rules — things like comma usage, apostrophes, semicolons, and subject-verb agreement — grouped by rule type, where each rule has a short plain-English explanation and a clear example sentence, so I can find the rule I need fast when I'm proofreading something.
